source.title: Assessing Generalization of SGD via Disagreement
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Vaishnavh Nagarajan; Christina Baek; J. Kolter

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figures are included without recoverable point values.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures disagreement as a proxy for test error and reports how their relationship varies across stochasticity sources, datasets, and distribution shifts. This is a conceptual measurement of generalization behavior, but it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern whether disagreement tracks test error, a behavior not named by V1–V8. It does not test random-label memorization, the listed architecture/optimizer/regularization comparisons, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples. The hyperparameter-sweep scatter plots and their correlation values are reported in figures; the text describes the relationship but does not give each point's values. Cited results from prior work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether prediction disagreement estimates test error and whether ensemble calibration explains that relationship. These are different claims from V1–V8. Its width and batch-size sweeps do not report the controlled trends required by V2 or V5; its architecture experiments do not establish the comparison required by V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors find approximate disagreement–test-error equality even for runs sharing training data, and prove that class-aggregated ensemble calibration is sufficient for equality in expectation. They do not explain when calibration arises, and calibration is not necessary for equality. Single-pair concentration remains incompletely explained; Appendix D.9 additionally finds that averaging four pairs reduces normalized estimation deviation from 0.112 to 0.034.
record.recipe_differences: Measures pairwise disagreement between independently trained models as an estimate of test error; it does not apply the interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationship varies with stochasticity source: AllDiff and DiffData are closer to equality than DiffInit and DiffOrder. The text reports deviations under PACS distribution shifts, with pretrained models satisfying the approximate relationship except for three source-target pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise disagreement approximates test error in the tested image-classification settings, with larger discrepancies for some stochasticity sources and distribution shifts. For example, R1 reports error 0.336 and disagreement 0.348; R10 reports 0.7180 and 0.2497.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction disagreement between independently trained models can estimate test error on unlabeled data, with accuracy depending on training stochasticity and evaluation distribution.

record.problems: Disagreement is compared with test error, but the study does not establish why calibration holds in practice. The authors say verifying calibration would require labeled test data, and that CACE is only a loose upper bound. Single-pair agreement is surprising even though two-model ensembles are poorly calibrated. Some reported scatter plots are figure-only. Table 2 has a caption/model-name mismatch, and its printed gap values include values inconsistent with subtracting the displayed error and disagreement.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports numerous additional PACS source-target combinations in Table 2 and figure-based hyperparameter sweeps in Figures 1–4, 10, and 13. Only four PACS combinations with large deviations were extracted as separate rows; the remaining table combinations were omitted to keep the record concise. Figure-only sweep points and correlation coefficients were not made into rows because values cannot be assigned to individual model conditions from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
The direction of test-error changes with width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and the effects of tuning or optimizer adaptations.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed against V1–V8, so cannot_determine does not dispute the reported measurements. The additional PACS combinations and figure-based sweeps are declared in rows_left_out and do not establish a listed version; no missing version-relevant rows are identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of training–test gaps.
Removing examples that are most memorized and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
